title: Cosmos DB Consistency and Distribution
description: Choose between strong, bounded staleness, session, consistent prefix, and eventual consistency for global Cosmos DB deployments.

data.text: Consistency describes how fresh reads are relative to writes in a distributed database. Cosmos DB offers **five tunable consistency levels** so you can trade off latency, availability, and consistency based on your application's needs. This is a key advantage over most distributed databases that force a single choice.

rows: Linearizability — reads always return the latest committed write
Reads are within a fixed number of versions or time behind writes
Within a client session, reads follow your own writes
Replicas converge eventually, no ordering guarantee

data.text: When you enable multiple regions, Cosmos DB replicates data transparently. Reads are served from the nearest region (or a preferred region list), while writes go to the write region. Switching the write region or enabling multi-master writes changes how consistency and conflicts are handled.

data.title: Set Consistency Level with Azure CLI
data.content: Change the default consistency for a Cosmos DB account
data.code:
az cosmosdb update \
  --name cosmos-demo \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --default-consistency-level BoundedStaleness \
  --max-staleness-prefix 100 \
  --max-interval-in-seconds 5

data.title: Enable Multi-Region Writes
data.content: Allow writes to multiple regions with the Azure CLI
data.code:
az cosmosdb update \
  --name cosmos-demo \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --enable-multiple-write-locations true

terms.definition: A configurable guarantee about how recent a read is relative to the latest write.
The single Azure region that accepts writes in a single-master account.
A configuration that accepts writes in multiple regions, using automatic conflict resolution.
The mechanism that resolves write conflicts in multi-master accounts, typically last-writer-wins.

data.title: Session Consistency Is the Safe Default
data.text: For most web and mobile apps, session consistency gives the best balance. Users always see their own writes, and latency remains low because reads can come from any nearby region.

data.title: Exercise: Choose Consistency for Scenarios
data.description: Match consistency levels to real-world requirements.
steps: Read the five consistency levels and their tradeoffs.
For each scenario below, pick a consistency level and explain your reasoning:
a) A banking app that must never show stale account balances.
b) A global news site where slight staleness is acceptable.
c) A chat app where users must see their own messages immediately.
d) An IoT dashboard that aggregates sensor data every minute.
data.expectedOutcome: A justified consistency choice for each scenario with reasoning about latency, availability, and consistency.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Cosmos DB offers five tunable consistency levels.
Strong consistency guarantees the latest writes but has the highest latency.
Session consistency is the best default for user-facing apps.
Global distribution adds regions without schema changes or code changes.
data.takeaway: Consistency is a choice in Cosmos DB, not a limitation. Pick the level that matches your app's correctness requirements.
